issues.legal_issue: A claimant’s established right to enjoy land without liability for assessment is an interest in property modified to the claimant’s disadvantage when abolition of a jagir makes the land assessable.
material_facts: The claimant held, under a compromise decree, the right to own and possess certain Gharkhed lands free from assessment.
After the jagir was abolished, the lands became liable to assessment under the Act.
The claimant was not the jagirdar, and compensation for this modification had not been provided under the Act.
issues.conclusion: The claimant was entitled to claim compensation under section 14(1) for the modification of his interest in the lands.
issues.legal_principle: Section 14(1) permits a person other than a jagirdar to apply for compensation when the Act abolishes, extinguishes or modifies that person’s right to or interest in property and the Act provides no compensation for that change. Section 4 made jagir villages liable to land revenue. Enjoying land free from assessment is more valuable than enjoying it subject to assessment, so imposing assessment modifies the holder’s interest to his disadvantage. The Court distinguished State of Gujarat v. Vakhatsinghji Sursinghji Vaghela, where reduced assessment had been a concession rather than an established right, and explained Shapurji Jivanji v. Collector of Bombay as recognizing that the right to collect assessment may be relinquished by contract or legislation.

rule.if: compensation_claim_under_jagir_abolition_law and claimant_is_not_jagirdar and land_was_enjoyed_free_of_assessment_as_an_established_right and abolition_made_the_land_assessable and no_compensation_was_provided_for_the_change

predicates.compensation_claim_under_jagir_abolition: A person sought compensation for a change to a property interest caused by a law abolishing jagirs.
predicates.claimant_is_not_jagirdar: The person seeking compensation was not the jagirdar.
predicates.land_was_enjoyed_free_of_assessment_as_a: The claimant held and exercised an established right to enjoy land without paying assessment.
predicates.abolition_made_the_land_assessable: Following abolition, the land became subject to assessment payable by the claimant.
predicates.no_compensation_was_provided_for_the_cha: The law provided no compensation for the change to the claimant’s property interest.

issues.definition: When a non-jagirdar seeking compensation for a property change caused by jagir abolition held an established right to enjoy land free of assessment, abolition made the land assessable, and no compensation was provided for the change, the claimant may claim compensation for the modified property interest.

issues.legal_issue: A right to receive a recurring allowance from a jagir that is charged on the jagir is an interest in property extinguished by abolition of the jagir.
material_facts: The claimant had, under a compromise decree, the right to receive an annual cash allowance from the jagir.
The allowance was payable from the jagir and was a charge on it, rather than a personal liability of the jagirdar.
Abolition of the jagir extinguished that interest, and the Act provided no compensation for it.
issues.conclusion: The claimant was entitled to claim compensation under section 14(1) for the extinguished interest represented by the cash allowance.
issues.legal_principle: Section 14(1) permits a person other than a jagirdar to apply for compensation when the Act abolishes, extinguishes or modifies that person’s right to or interest in property and the Act provides no compensation for that change. A right to receive an allowance charged on the jagir is an interest in property; extinguishing it through abolition therefore falls within the section.
